zh: “你吃了饭没有？”“吃过。”阿巧姐说，“一直想吃陆稿荐的酱猪肉，今天总算到口了。”说着，她服侍他卸衣洗脚，一面问起何桂清那里的情形。胡雪岩不便将那些如何进京活动调任的话告诉她，但除此以外，就没有什么可说的了，因为何家的内眷亲属，他一个也不曾看到。等上了床，阿巧姐在枕头上问他：“明天怎么样？想到哪里去？”“正事都办完了。明天哪里去逛一天？到苏州一趟，总不能说虎丘都不曾到过。”听他这一说，阿巧姐颇有意外之感，“我原以为你的事，总得有几天，才能办完。”她说，“这一来……”“怎么呢？”胡雪岩见她欲言又止，同样地感到诧异。“我本来想回木渎去一趟。现在看来不成功了。”“这倒无所谓。”胡雪岩问，“你去干什么？”“ 咦，你这话问得怪！我家在木渎，到了苏州不回去，说得过去吗？”“喔！”胡雪岩脱口说：“你是去看老公？”“说得可要难听！”阿巧姐有些气急败坏地，“我是回娘家。”
en: “Have you eaten?” “Yes,” A’qiao replied. “I've been wanting some of Lugaojian's pork in soy sauce for ages. Today I finally had it.” As she helped him undress and wash his feet, she asked what had happened at He Guiqing's. Hu could hardly tell her about going to the capital to seek a transfer, and apart from that there was little to say. He had not seen a single member of He's family. Once they were in bed, she asked from her pillow, “What about tomorrow? Where would you like to go?” “The business is finished. Where shall we spend the day? I can't come all the way to Suzhou and say I haven't even seen Tiger Hill.” This surprised her. “I thought your business would take several days. In that case...” “What is it?” Her hesitation surprised him in turn. “I'd meant to go home to Mudu. Now it seems I can't.” “That needn't matter. What do you want to do there?” “What an odd question! My home's in Mudu. How could I come to Suzhou and not go back?” “Oh!” Hu blurted out. “You're going to see your husband?” “Must you put it so unpleasantly?” She was flustered and angry. “I'm going to my parents' home.”

zh: 看她的神气，这不是假话，既然如此，胡雪岩觉得倒不妨问了下去：“你娘家还有什么人？”“娘老子，一个兄弟。”阿巧姐又说，“我看一看他们，有点钱带到了，马上回城。”“那得多少时候？”“一来一去，总要两天。”“两天？”胡雪岩想了想说，“你明天就去，后天回来，一回来我们就走。”“这样，”阿巧姐歉然他说，“明天不能陪你逛虎丘了。”“这倒无所谓。阿巧，”胡雪岩问道，“你跟你夫家，到底怎么回事？”“怎么回事？只要有钱给他们，他们啥也不管。”阿巧姐用这样鄙夷不屑的口吻回答。“钱是按月带回去？”“有时一个月，有时两个月。钱多多带，钱少少带，没有一定。再也要看有没有便人。常常要托人，真麻烦。”“与其如此，还不如一刀两断，也省得托人麻烦。”阿巧姐不响，看样子是有些为难，胡雪岩便在猜度她的为难是什么？“一刀两断是可以，就怕他们狮子大开口。”“你倒说说看，大到怎样的程度？乡下人开口来也不见大到哪里去。”“总要两千银子。”
en: From her expression, she appeared to be telling the truth. Hu felt he might as well ask further. “Who's left in your family?” “My mother and a brother. I'll see them, take them a little money and come straight back to the city.” “How long would that take?” “Two days for the journey there and back.” “Two days?” He considered. “Go tomorrow, then, and return the day after. We'll leave as soon as you're back.” “Then I shan't be able to go to Tiger Hill with you tomorrow,” she said apologetically. “That doesn't matter. A’qiao, what exactly is the arrangement between you and your husband's family?” “What arrangement? So long as I give them money, they don't care about anything.” Her tone was contemptuous. “Do you send money every month?” “Sometimes every month, sometimes every two months. More when I have more, less when I have less. There's no fixed rule. It also depends on finding someone going that way. Always having to ask people is a real nuisance.” “Wouldn't it be better to make a clean break? That would save you the trouble.” She said nothing and seemed troubled. Hu wondered what the difficulty was. “A clean break is possible. I'm afraid they'll demand an outrageous sum.” “How outrageous? Country people can hardly ask for very much.” “It would take at least two thousand taels.”

zh: 两千银子倒是狮子大开口了，在上海“长三”中，娶个红倌人也不过花到这个数目，而阿巧姐人虽不错，身价到底不值这么多。如果说一句“两千就两千”，这样出手，不能博得豪阔之名，倒有些象洋场新流行的俗语，成了“洋盘”。当然，这是因为从阿巧姐情不自禁地表现出对“何老爷”有“意思”以后，胡雪岩对她的兴趣已经打了折扣之故，否则他就不会有那样做“洋盘”的感觉。于是他淡淡地答了句：“到了上海再说吧，手边也没有这么多银子。”其实他带着三千银票，这样说是托词，阿巧姐原不曾作此期待，因而也不觉得失望。一宿无话，第二天起身，他实践前宵枕上的许诺，催阿巧姐回木渎。“丢你一个人在客栈里，真不好意思。”阿巧姐说，“要么，你跟我一同去。”这算什么名堂？乡下风气闭塞，阿巧姐这样带个“野汉子”回家，就算她自己不在乎，胡雪岩也觉得尴尬，所以摇着手说：“不要紧，不要紧！你一个人去好了。一个人在城里逛逛也很好。”“那么，我明天一早就动身回来。大概中午就可以到了。”说着，便托金阊栈代为雇一顶来回的轿子，胡雪岩想想让她空手回去，自己一无表示，也不好意思，便取了一张一百两的银票，说是送她父母买补药吃。阿巧姐自然高兴，上轿时便越发有那种依依不舍的神情了。
en: Two thousand was indeed an outrageous demand. Even marrying a celebrated courtesan from a changsan house in Shanghai would cost no more. Fine woman though A’qiao was, her value in such a transaction did not amount to that. If he simply said, “Then two thousand it shall be,” he would not win a reputation for generosity. He would look like what the foreign settlement's new slang called a gullible customer. Of course, he felt this way because his interest in her had diminished since she involuntarily betrayed her feelings for “Mr He.” Otherwise, the thought of being made a fool of would not have arisen. “We'll discuss it when we get back to Shanghai,” he answered coolly. “I haven't that much money with me.” In fact, he carried three thousand taels in banknotes. It was an excuse. A’qiao had expected no such offer, however, and was not disappointed. The night passed without further incident. In the morning, Hu kept his promise of the night before and urged her to go to Mudu. “I feel bad leaving you alone at the inn. Why don't you come with me?” What sort of arrangement would that be? Country customs were restrictive. Even if she did not mind bringing a lover home, Hu would feel embarrassed. He waved the suggestion aside. “Never mind. Go on your own. I shall enjoy looking round the city by myself.” “Then I'll set out early tomorrow morning. I should be back about noon.” She asked Jinchang Inn to hire a sedan chair for the return journey. Hu felt it would be rather shabby to let her go empty-handed without making any gesture himself. He took out a hundred-tael note, saying it was for her parents to buy nourishing medicines. Naturally delighted, she seemed still more reluctant to part when she got into the chair.

zh: 也不过是她刚走，何桂清又派人送了柬贴来，约他午间在狮子林小酌。胡雪岩正愁无处可去，自然是欣然许诺，给了回片，发了赏钱，坐轿进阊门，到玄妙观里喝了一碗茶，在庙市上买了几样小件的玉器，到了近午时分，就在庙前雇一顶小轿，去赴何桂清之约。狮子林以假山出名，据说是倪云林亲手所经营，曲折高下，诡异莫测，何桂清亲自引导游览，随处指点，极其殷勤。一圈逛下来，去了个把钟头，走得累了，便觉得饮食格外有味，吃到半饱，话才多了起来。这种场合，自然不宜谈官场，谈商场则何桂清是外行，于是只好谈山水、谈风月了。有了几分酒意的何桂清，谈兴愈豪，话也更小顾忌，一谈谈到家庭，他忽然说道：“雪岩兄，我有件事，要腼颜奉托。内人体弱多病，性情又最贤慧，常劝我置一房妾侍，可以为她分劳，照料我的饮食起居。我倒也觉得有此必要，只是在江苏做官，纳部民为妾，大于禁例。这一次进京，沿途得要个贴身的人照料，不知道你能不能替我在上海或者在杭州，物色一个？”“这容易得很。请云公说说看，喜欢怎样的人？”“就象阿巧姐那样的，使是上选。”何桂清脱口而答。
en: She had scarcely left when He Guiqing sent another invitation, this time to lunch at the Lion Grove Garden. Hu had been wondering where to go and gladly accepted. He sent back a reply, tipped the messenger and took a sedan chair through Chang Gate. After drinking a bowl of tea at Xuanmiao Temple and buying a few small jade objects at the temple market, he hired another small chair outside the temple shortly before noon and went to keep the appointment. The Lion Grove was famous for its rockery, said to have been designed by Ni Yunlin himself. Its paths twisted, rose and fell in strange, unpredictable ways. He personally conducted Hu through it, pointing out its features with the utmost attentiveness. A circuit took about an hour and left them tired enough to find the food especially good. Only after they had eaten a fair amount did conversation become lively. Official affairs were unsuitable for such an occasion, and He knew nothing of commerce, so they talked of scenery and romantic pleasures. With a little wine in him, He grew more expansive and less guarded. When they reached the subject of family, he suddenly said, “Brother Xueyan, there's something I must ask, though I'm embarrassed to do so. My wife is frail and often ill, and she has the most generous disposition. She frequently urges me to take a concubine who could share her burdens and attend to my meals and daily needs. I do see the necessity. But as an official serving in Jiangsu, I am strictly forbidden to take a woman under my jurisdiction as a concubine. On this journey to the capital, I shall need someone close to look after me. Could you find a suitable woman for me in Shanghai or Hangzhou?” “Nothing could be easier. Tell me what sort of woman you like.” “Someone like A’qiao would be ideal,” He answered without thinking.

zh: 胡雪岩一愣，细看一看他的脸色，不象饰词巧索，心里使好过些了，“我知道了。”他点点头，“总在云公动身以前，我必有以报命。”“拜托，拜托！”何桂清说，“回头我先送五百两银子过来。请雪岩兄在这个数目之内替我办。”“用不了这么多。”胡雪岩说：“云公也不必送来，办成了，我跟云公一起算，顺便还要讨赏。”“言重，言重！该我谢媒。”答应是答应下来了，回到金阊栈，细想一想，要找象阿巧姐这样的人，却真还不大容易。“嗐！我傻了！”胡雪岩突破心头的蔽境，解决了难题，却带来怅然若失的情怀。何必再去寻阿巧姐这样的人？阿巧姐不就在眼前？然而胡雪岩这一次撒手，跟放弃阿珠的感觉不大相同，当时移花接木将阿珠与陈世龙之间的那条红丝联系起来，不但心安理得，而且有快心惬意之感，如今要将阿巧姐送入别人的怀抱，心里却是酸溜溜的，很不好受。因此一个人徘徊又徘徊，翻来覆去的在想，除此以外可还有更好的办法？
en: Hu started. Studying He's expression, he concluded that this did not seem to be a disguised request for A’qiao herself, and felt somewhat better. “I understand,” he said, nodding. “Before you leave, I shall certainly have something to report.” “Thank you! I'll send five hundred taels over presently. Please arrange it within that sum.” “It won't cost so much. Nor need you send the money. Once it's settled, we'll reckon everything together. I'll even ask for a reward.” “You put it too strongly. I ought to thank my matchmaker.” Hu had agreed, but back at Jinchang Inn he realized that finding another woman like A’qiao would be no easy matter. “Ah! How foolish I've been!” Breaking through the obstruction in his mind, he solved the difficulty, only to be left with a sense of loss. Why seek someone like A’qiao when A’qiao herself was already there? Yet letting her go felt different from giving up A’zhu. When he had redirected the match, joining A’zhu's red thread of marriage to Chen Shilong's, his conscience had been clear and he had felt positively pleased. Now, at the thought of sending A’qiao into another man's arms, his heart was sour with unhappiness. He paced back and forth, turning the matter over repeatedly. Was there no better way?

zh: 这样蚁旋磨转的一直到天快黑，听得外面有人在喊：“胡大老爷！”声音很熟，却一时想不起是谁？出门一看，才影绰绰的辨清楚，是周一鸣。“中午我来伺候，胡大老爷出去了？”“喔，对不起，失迎！”胡雪岩答道：“何学台约我逛狮子林。”“姨太太也不在？”“她回木渎去了。”胡雪岩又补了一句：“那不是小妾，你的称呼用不着。”这也算是碰了一个钉子，周一鸣答不上来了，没话找话说了句：“胡大老爷怎不点灯？”“啊！”胡雪岩这时才醒悟，自己也觉得好笑，说了一半实话：“我大想一件心事，想得出神了。老周，我们吃酒去。”“是！”周一鸣赔笑说道：“我本来就打算做个小东，请胡大老爷喝杯酒。只怕胡大老爷不肯赏脸，不敢说。”“笑话！啥叫不肯赏脸？你说得太客气了。”胡雪岩很中意周一鸣，想跟他谈谈，便很恳切的说：“我扰你的。不过，下馆子我可不去，不是怕你多花饯。第一，中午油腻吃得太多，第二，想看看苏州的小酒店是怎么个光景，跟我们杭州有什么不同。”“胡大老爷这样说，我就恭敬不如从命了。这种专门吃酒的酒店，玄妙观前多得很，地方很干净，可以坐一坐。““那好，我们就走吧！”
en: His thoughts went round and round like an ant circling a millstone until it was almost dark. Then someone called from outside, “Mr Hu!” The voice was familiar, though for a moment he could not place it. Going out, he dimly made out Zhou Yiming. “When I called at noon, you were out?” “Oh, I'm sorry to have missed you. Education Commissioner He invited me to the Lion Grove.” “And the young mistress is away too?” “She's gone home to Mudu. She isn't my concubine, by the way. There's no need to call her that.” This was something of a rebuff. Zhou could find no answer and said, merely to fill the silence, “Why haven't you lit a lamp?” “Ah!” Only now did Hu notice. Amused at himself, he gave half the truth. “I've been so absorbed in something on my mind that I forgot. Old Zhou, let's go for a drink.” “Certainly.” Zhou smiled ingratiatingly. “I'd been hoping to act as host and offer you a cup, but I was afraid you wouldn't honour me and didn't dare suggest it.” “Nonsense! Why wouldn't I? You're far too polite.” Hu liked him and wanted to talk, so he added earnestly, “I'll be your guest. But I won't go to a restaurant. It isn't that I'm afraid of making you spend too much. First, I've had too much rich food at lunch. Second, I'd like to see what Suzhou's little taverns are like and how they differ from Hangzhou's.” “Then I'll do as you say. There are plenty of places devoted to drinking in front of Xuanmiao Temple. They're clean, and we could sit awhile.” “Good. Let's go.”

zh: 胡雪岩随手套上一件马褂，关照店伙计锁了门，与周一鸣雇了一辆马车进城。玄妙观前灯火辉煌，十分热闹，江宁失守，苏州成了全省的首善之区，文武官员，平空添了数百，大多不曾带家眷，公余无处可去，多集中在玄妙观前，闲逛的闲逛，买醉的买醉，市面要到二更才罢。酒店家家客满，最后在一家字号叫“元大昌”的。找到了一副临街的座头，两个人坐下来，要了绍兴花雕，随即便有两三个青布衣衫，收拾得十分干净挺括的上了年纪的妇人，挽着篮来卖下酒的卤菜。那些鸭头和鸭翅膀，看样子很不坏，但味道不怎么样，好在胡雪岩旨在领略苏州酒店的情趣，不在口腹，倒也不甚介意。等坐定了，吃过一巡酒，他放眼四顾，开始观察，苏州本地人雍容揖让，文文气气，一望而知，他们问壁一桌就是，两个都是白须老者，但一口道地的苏州话，却是其软无比，只听他们高谈阔论，也是一种乐趣。四外烽火连天，这“元大昌”中却是酒温语软，充满了逸兴闲情，隔座那两位白须老者，谈的是嘉庆年问的旧话，谈砚台、谈宜兴的“供春壶”、谈竹雕，都是太平盛世、文人墨客的雅玩。
en: Hu slipped on an outer jacket, told an inn servant to lock his door and hired a carriage with Zhou to go into the city. The area before Xuanmiao Temple blazed with lights and bustled with people. Since Jiangning had fallen, Suzhou had become the province's foremost city. Several hundred civil and military officials had appeared almost overnight. Most had not brought their families and had nowhere to go when work was done. They congregated here, some strolling, others drinking themselves tipsy, and the market remained busy until the second watch. Every tavern was full. At last they found seats facing the street in one called Yuandachang. They sat down and ordered Shaoxing huadiao. Two or three older women, neatly and cleanly dressed in blue cotton, promptly approached with baskets of braised snacks to accompany the wine. The duck heads and wings looked good enough, though their flavour was unremarkable. But Hu had come to savour the atmosphere of a Suzhou tavern, not its food, and did not much mind. Once settled, after their first round of wine, he looked about him and began to observe. Suzhou natives were easily recognized by their composed manners, courteous deference and scholarly air. The two men at the next table were examples: both white-bearded, both speaking the local dialect in wonderfully soft voices. Merely listening to their animated conversation was a pleasure. War blazed on every side, yet Yuandachang was full of warm wine, gentle voices and leisurely enjoyment. The two old men were recalling the Jiaqing years, discussing inkstones, Yixing Gongchun teapots and bamboo carvings—the elegant playthings of scholars in a peaceful, prosperous age.

zh: “人生在世，为什么？”胡雪岩忽生感慨，“就是吃吃喝喝过一生？”这句话问得周一鸣直着眼好愣，不但不能回答，甚至也无从了解他的意思。“我是说，象隔壁那两位老太爷，”胡雪岩放低了声音说：“大概是靠收租过日子的乡绅。这样的人家，我们杭州也很多，祖上做过官，挣下一批田地，如果不是出了个败家精，安分度日，总有一两代好吃。本身也总有个把功名，好一点是进过学的秀才，不然就是二三十两银子捐来的监生，也算场面上的人物。一年到头无事忙，白天孵茶馆，晚上‘摆一碗’，逍遥自在到六七十岁，一口气不来，回老家见阎王，说是我阳世里走过一遭了。问他阳世里做点啥？啥也不做！象这样的人，做鬼都没有意思。“这番不知是自嘲，还是调侃他人的话，周一鸣倒是听懂了，此人也算是有志向的人，所以对胡雪岩的话，颇有同感，“是阿！”他说，“人生在世，总要做一番事业，才对得起父母。”
en: “What is a man alive for?” Hu asked, suddenly moved. “Simply to eat and drink his way through life?” Zhou stared blankly. He could not answer; he could scarcely even understand the question. “I mean people like those two old gentlemen,” Hu explained, lowering his voice. “They're probably country gentry living on rents. We have plenty of such families in Hangzhou. An ancestor held office and acquired some land. Unless a spendthrift appears, quiet living leaves enough to feed a generation or two. The men themselves generally have some examination standing. The better ones are licentiates admitted to the schools; otherwise they've paid twenty or thirty taels for the status of an Imperial Academy student. They count as people of standing too. All year round they're busy doing nothing: they sit in teahouses by day and have a bowl of wine at night. They drift pleasantly on until sixty or seventy, then stop breathing and go home to meet the King of Hell. ‘I've had my turn in the world of the living,’ they say. Ask what they did there, and the answer is nothing! Even being a ghost would be meaningless for someone like that.” Whether he was mocking himself or teasing others was unclear, but Zhou understood this much. He too had ambitions and felt considerable sympathy. “Quite so. A man should accomplish something in his lifetime, if only to do right by his parents.”

zh: 有这句话，胡雪岩觉得可以跟他谈谈了，“老周，”他问，“听说你在水师，也是蛮有名的人物。”“名是谈不到，人缘是不错。”周一鸣喝了口酒，满腹牢骚地说，“从前船户都叫我‘老总’，见了客气得很，现在都叫我老周，啥跑腿的事都要干。想想真不是味道。”“你的意思，仍旧想回水师？”“想也不行！”周一鸣摇摇头，“从前我那个长官，现在官更大了，听了他娘的小舅子的话，把我恨得要死。要想再回去补个名字，除非移名改姓，从小兵干起，那要干到什么时候才得出头？想想只好算了。”“果真你要回去，我倒可以帮你的忙。”胡雪岩说，“想来水师管带，官也不会大到哪里去，我替你请何学台写封信，你看怎么样？”“求得到何学台的信，我又不必回原地方了，何学台跟江苏巡抚许大人是同年，有何学台的信，我投到‘抚标’去当差，比原来的差使好得多。”“那好！”胡雪岩说，“这上头我不大懂。明天我带你去见何学台，你当面跟他说。”听得这话，再想到何桂清对胡雪岩的客气，料知他们交情极深，事必有济，所以他极其兴奋，连连道谢，应酬得格外殷勤了。
en: At that, Hu felt they could talk. “Old Zhou, I hear you were quite a figure in the navy.” “I wouldn't say I had a name, but I got on well with people.” Zhou took a drink and poured out his grievance. “Boatmen used to call me ‘Officer’ and treat me with great respect. Now it's ‘Old Zhou’, and I have to run every kind of errand. It leaves a bitter taste.” “You'd like to return to the navy, then?” “Wishing won't help.” He shook his head. “My old commanding officer has risen higher still. He listened to that damned brother-in-law of his and hates me like poison. The only way to get back on the rolls would be to change my name and start again as a common soldier. How long would it take to get anywhere? I can only give it up.” “If you really want to go back, I could help. A naval commander can hardly be so very high an official. What if I asked Education Commissioner He to write a letter for you?” “With a letter from him, I wouldn't have to return to my old place. He and Governor Xu of Jiangsu passed the metropolitan examination in the same year. I could enter the troops under the governor's direct command. That would be far better than my old post.” “Very well. I don't know much about these things. Tomorrow I'll take you to see the commissioner, and you can tell him yourself.” Remembering how courteously He had treated Hu, Zhou concluded that they must be close friends and that success was assured. He was intensely excited, thanked Hu repeatedly and became still more attentive as host.

zh: 酒吃到六分，胡雪岩不想再喝，叫了两碗“双浇面”，一碗是焖得稀烂的大肉面，一碗是熏鱼面，两下对换，有鱼有肉，吃得酒醉饭饱，花不到五钱银子，胡雪岩深为满意。“钱不在多，只要会用。”他说，“吃得象今天这么舒服的日子，我还不多。”“这是因为胡大老爷晓得我做东，没有好东西吃，心里先就有打算了，所以说好。”“这就叫‘知足常乐’。”胡雪岩说，“凡事能够退一步想，就没有烦恼了。”这天晚上他再想阿巧姐的去留，就是持着这种态度，譬如不曾遇见她，譬如她香消玉殒了，譬如她为豪客所夺，这样每自譬一次，便将阿巧姐看得谈了些，最后终于下了决心，自己说一声：“君子成人之美！”然后叹口气，蒙头大睡。
en: When Hu had reached a comfortable degree of tipsiness, he wanted no more wine. They ordered two bowls of noodles with a double topping between them: one came with pork braised until meltingly tender, the other with smoked fish. By exchanging toppings, they each had fish and meat. They ate and drank to their hearts' content for less than half a tael. Hu was thoroughly pleased. “It isn't how much money you have, but how you use it. I've seldom enjoyed a meal as much as this.” “That's because you knew I was treating you and expected nothing fine. You'd prepared yourself, so it seems good.” “That's what they mean by ‘contentment brings lasting happiness’. If you can step back a little in your thinking, there's nothing to trouble you.” That night, he approached the question of letting A’qiao go in this same spirit. Suppose he had never met her. Suppose she had died. Suppose some powerful patron had taken her from him. Each such reflection loosened his attachment a little. At last he made up his mind. “A gentleman helps others attain their happiness,” he told himself. Then he sighed, pulled the quilt over his head and went to sleep.

zh: 第二天一早起身，周一鸣已经在等着了，临时客串听差，替他奔走招呼，所以阿巧姐虽不在身边，胡雪岩亦觉得并无不便。同时心里在想，自己一向为求使捷爽利，不喜欢带个听差在身边，看来若有象同一鸣这样的人，带在身边，亦自不妨，这一趟回去，或在杭州，或在上海，倒要好好物色一个。等他漱洗完毕，周一鸣又要请他进城去喝早茶。胡雪岩心里有数，便连声答道：“好的，好的！吃完早茶，我带你去见何学台，当面求他替你写信。”于是进了城在“吴苑”茶店吃早茶。苏州的茶店跟杭州的又不同，杭州的茶店，大都是敞厅，一视同仁，不管是缙绅先生，还是贩夫走卒，入座都是顾客，苏州的茶店，分出等级，各不相淆，胡雪岩好热闹，与周一鸣只在最外面那间厅上坐，一面喝茶，一面吃各式各样的点心，消磨到十点钟，看看是时候了，算了帐，安步当车到苏州府学去见何桂清。由于爱屋及乌的缘故，何桂清对周一鸣也很客气，再三让坐，周一鸣守着官场的规矩，只是垂手肃立，最后却不过意，才屁股沾着椅子边，仿佛蹲着似地坐了下来。看他这局促的光景，胡雪岩倒觉得于心不忍，便要言不烦他说明来意，何桂清当时答道：“许大人亲自到上海督师去了。”接着转脸问胡雪岩：“现在倒有个好机会，是去收税，不知道这位周君愿意不愿意屈就。”“屈就这两个字言重了。不知是哪一处税卡？”“现在新创一种‘厘金’，你总晓得。”“这听说过。”胡雪岩答道，“到底怎么回事，却还不十分清楚。”
en: When he rose early the next morning, Zhou was already waiting. Acting as a temporary servant, he ran about attending to Hu's needs, so that even without A’qiao Hu felt no inconvenience. He had always preferred travelling without a servant for the sake of freedom and efficiency. But a man like Zhou might be useful to have beside him. On his return, whether in Hangzhou or Shanghai, he ought to look carefully for someone suitable. After Hu had washed, Zhou invited him into the city for morning tea. Understanding what was on his mind, Hu readily agreed. “Yes, yes. Afterwards, I'll take you to the commissioner and ask him in person for a letter.” They went to the Wuyuan teahouse. Suzhou teahouses differed from Hangzhou's. In Hangzhou, most had open halls and treated everyone alike. Gentry, pedlars and labourers were all customers once seated. In Suzhou, the different classes were separated and did not mingle. Hu enjoyed a crowd, so he and Zhou sat in the outermost hall, drinking tea and sampling the various pastries until ten. Judging the time right, they paid and strolled to the prefectural school to see He Guiqing. Out of regard for Hu, He treated Zhou courteously too, repeatedly asking him to sit. Zhou observed official etiquette, standing respectfully with his hands at his sides. At last he could not refuse and perched on the edge of a chair as though squatting. Hu felt sorry for his discomfort and explained their purpose briefly. “Governor Xu has gone to Shanghai to direct the troops in person,” He replied. Then he turned to Hu. “There is a good opening at present, though. It's tax collection. I wonder whether Mr Zhou would consider it beneath him.” “You flatter him. At which tax station?” “You've heard of the new levy called lijin?” “I've heard of it, but I don't yet know exactly how it works.”

zh: “是你们浙江的一个奇士的策划。此人算来是雪轩的部民，湖州府长兴人，名叫钱江……”钱江字东平，是浙江长兴的一名监生，好大言，多奇计，仿佛战国的策士一流人物。鸦片战争一起，协办大学士吏部尚书，宗室奕经，奉旨以“杨威将军”的名义，到浙江督办军务，钱江叩辕献计，招募壮士，奇袭英军，擒其首脑。畏葸的奕经，如何敢用这样的奇计？敬谢不敏。后来林则徐得罪遣戍，而钱江在广州主张拒英，亦充军到伊犁，在戍所相遇，林则徐对他深为赏识。当林则徐遇赦进关时，设法将他洗脱了罪，带入关内，在京城里为他揄扬于公卿之间，声名鹊起，不幸地，林则徐不久病殁，钱江顿失凭依，于是挟策游于江淮之间，在扬州遇到了雷以诚。献上两策，第一策是预领空白捐照，随时填发，第二策就是开办厘金。
en: “It was devised by a remarkable man from your own Zhejiang. Indeed, he comes from Xuexuan's jurisdiction: Changxing County in Huzhou Prefecture. His name is Qian Jiang.” Qian Jiang, courtesy name Dongping, was an Imperial Academy student from Changxing. Fond of bold talk and ingenious schemes, he resembled the wandering strategists of the Warring States. When the Opium War began, Yijing, an imperial clansman who was assistant grand secretary and president of the Board of Civil Appointments, received orders to direct military affairs in Zhejiang as General Who Spreads Awe. Qian presented himself at his headquarters with a plan: recruit brave men, surprise the British and capture their leaders. Timid Yijing dared not attempt such an extraordinary scheme and politely declined. Later, Lin Zexu fell into disgrace and was sent into exile. Qian, having advocated resistance to the British in Guangzhou, was likewise sentenced to military exile in Ili. They met there, and Lin greatly admired him. When Lin was pardoned and allowed to return within the passes, he arranged to clear Qian's conviction and brought him back. In the capital, Lin praised him among the high officials, and his reputation rapidly grew. Unfortunately, Lin died not long afterwards, leaving Qian without support. He then travelled with his schemes through the country between the Yangtze and Huai rivers. In Yangzhou, he met Lei Yixian and proposed two measures. The first was to obtain blank certificates for purchased ranks in advance, to be filled in and issued on the spot. The second was to introduce lijin.

zh: 穷了想富，富了想贵，人之常情，所以做生意发了财的，尤其是两淮的那班盐商，最喜欢捐官，捐到三品道员还觉得戴蓝顶子不够威风，总想找机会，如报效军需，捐助河工，花大把银子买个“特保”，弄个二品顶戴的红顶子才肯罢休。但是捐官的手续甚为繁复，吏部书办的花样百出，往往“上兑”一两年，一张证明几品官员身分的“部照”还拿不到，这一来自然影响捐官的兴趣。钱江的办法就是专为想过官瘾的富商打算，一手交钱，一手交货，上了兑，立刻填发部照，爽快无比。雷以諴认为此策极妙，便托钱江上了个奏折，细陈其事，照他的办法，部里的书办就没有好处了，所以起初部议不准。无奈国库空虚，乾嘉年间积下的上千万银子，从道光年间鸦片战争以来，以奕经、耆英、琦善以及赛尚阿等总领师干的钦差大臣，花得光光，现在朝廷为对付洪杨起义，“既要马儿好，又要马儿不吃草”，如果马儿自己觅草去吃，犹复不准，如何说得过去？因此，钱江的妙策，到底被批准了。部里领来大批的空白捐照，现款交易，而且没有层出不穷的小费，既快又便宜，捐官的人，自然趋之若鹜。雷以諴就靠了这笔收入，招募乡勇，才得扼守扬州、镇江一带。然而捐官只是一趟头的买卖，细水长流，还得另想别法，于是而有厘金。
en: The poor long to be rich, and the rich to be honoured: that is human nature. Merchants who had made fortunes, particularly the salt merchants of the Two Huai districts, were therefore especially fond of purchasing official rank. Even after contributing enough to become third-rank circuit intendants, they felt a blue finial insufficiently imposing. They were always seeking opportunities—funding military supplies, for instance, or contributing to river works—to spend large sums on a special recommendation. Only a second-rank red finial would satisfy them. Yet buying rank involved complicated procedures. Clerks at the Board of Civil Appointments had endless tricks. A man might remit his payment and still wait a year or two for the board's certificate establishing his rank. Naturally, this diminished enthusiasm. Qian's scheme catered precisely to wealthy merchants eager to taste official distinction: money in one hand, goods in the other. As soon as payment was made, the certificate would be completed and issued. Nothing could be more straightforward. Lei thought the proposal excellent and had Qian submit a memorial setting it out in detail. Since the scheme would deprive the board's clerks of their profits, the board initially rejected it. But the treasury was empty. The more than ten million taels accumulated under Qianlong and Jiaqing had been exhausted since the Opium War in the Daoguang reign by imperial commissioners commanding armies—Yijing, Qiying, Qishan, Saishang’a and others. Now, in confronting the uprising of Hong and Yang, the court wanted a good horse without having to feed it. If it forbade the horse even to find its own fodder, how could that be justified? Qian's ingenious proposal was therefore approved at last. Large quantities of blank certificates arrived from the board. Transactions were immediate and required none of the endless incidental fees. Quicker and cheaper, the new arrangement naturally drew crowds of buyers. With this revenue, Lei recruited local volunteers and was able to hold the Yangzhou–Zhenjiang area. But each sale of rank brought payment only once. A continuing stream required another source. Hence lijin.

zh: 清朝的行商税，本来只有关税一种。大宗税收是钱粮地丁，因为失地太多而收额大减，两淮的盐税，亦因为兵火的影响，销场不旺，弥补之道，就靠厘金，一钱抽一厘，看起来税额甚轻，但积少成多，为数可观。最先是由雷以諴在扬州仙女庙、邵伯镇等运河码头，设卡试办，成效不坏，朝廷因而正式降旨，命两江总督怡良、江苏巡抚许乃钊、漕运总督杨以增，在江南、江北各地试行捐厘助饷，以裕军需。听罢何桂清的陈述，胡雪岩对钱江其人，深为仰慕，颇想一见，但这是一时办不到的事，只好丢开，先替周一鸣作打算。“他是水师出身，运河、长江各码头，都是熟人。若得云公栽培，当差决不致误事，坍云公的台。”“我知道，我知道，看周君也是很能干的人，而况又是你的举荐，一定赏识不虚。”何桂清说，“我马上写信，请坐一坐！”说罢，他退入书房，亲笔写了一封信。何洼清虽未做到封疆大吏，督抚的派头已经很足，两张八行笺，写着胡桃大的字，按科名先后，称雷以諴为“前辈”。胡雪岩接了信代周一鸣道谢，周一鸣自己则叩头相谢。
en: Previously, the Qing had imposed only customs duties on travelling merchants. Its principal tax revenue came from the land and poll levy, but so much territory had been lost that receipts had fallen sharply. War had also depressed sales in the Two Huai salt market and reduced its tax yield. Lijin was to make up the shortfall: one li collected on every qian. The rate appeared slight, but small sums accumulated into a considerable amount. Lei first tried it at canal wharves such as Xiannümiao and Shaobo near Yangzhou. The results were good. The court then formally ordered Yiliang, Governor-General of Liangjiang, Xu Naizhao, Governor of Jiangsu, and Yang Yizeng, Director-General of Grain Transport, to introduce contributions of lijin for military funds in various places north and south of the Yangtze. After hearing He's account, Hu greatly admired Qian and longed to meet him. That was impossible for the moment, however, so he set the thought aside and returned to Zhou's prospects. “He served in the navy and knows people at wharves all along the canal and the Yangtze. If you give him this opportunity, he certainly won't neglect his duties or let you down.” “I know. Mr Zhou looks very capable, and with your recommendation I'm sure your confidence is justified. I'll write at once. Please sit awhile.” He withdrew to his study and wrote the letter himself. Though not yet a provincial ruler, he already had all the manner of a governor or governor-general. His characters, as large as walnuts, filled two sheets of eight-line letter paper. In keeping with the order of their examination success, he addressed Lei as his senior. Hu received the letter and thanked He for Zhou, who himself expressed his gratitude by kowtowing.

zh: “你先回去吧！”胡雪岩对周一鸣说，“我还要陪何大人谈谈。”等周一鸣一走，何桂清告诉胡雪岩一个消息，说江苏巡抚许乃钊有调动的消息，“今天一早，接到京里的密信。”他说，“我想等一等再说。”许乃钊调动，何以他要等候？细想一想，胡雪岩明白了，必是何桂清有接此任的可能，不妨静以观变。这个主意的变化，胡雪岩觉得对自己这方面大为不利，因而颇想劝他仍照原来的计划，先活动调任仓场侍郎，然后放到浙江去当巡抚，那一来，对王有龄，对自己，对嵇鹤龄便有左右逢源、诸事顺手之乐了。暗中的猜测，不便明劝，万一猜得不对，变成无的放矢，是件可笑的事，叫何桂清看轻了自己，而且凡事明说不如暗示，旁敲侧击的效果最好，这是胡雪岩所深知的。于是略想一想，有了一套说词。“江苏巡抚这个缺，从前是天下第一，现在，我看是最末等的了。”他忽然发了这样一段议论。何桂清当然要注意，“苏抚的缺分，不如以前是真的，”他说，“但亦不至于沧为末等。”“我是瞎说说的，跟云公请教。”胡雪岩徐徐而言，想着末等的理由，想到一条说一条：“第一是大乱在江苏，地方少了，钱粮也就少了。”
en: “Go back first,” Hu told Zhou. “I'll stay and talk with His Excellency.” Once Zhou had left, He told Hu that Xu Naizhao might be transferred from the governorship of Jiangsu. “A confidential letter from the capital arrived early this morning. I think I shall wait and see.” Why should Xu's transfer make him wait? After a moment, Hu understood: He must have a chance of succeeding him and wanted to observe developments. This change of plan would be decidedly unfavourable to Hu's side. He wanted to urge He to keep to the original course: first arrange a transfer as granary vice-minister, then seek appointment as governor of Zhejiang. That would make everything convenient for Wang Youling, Ji Heling and Hu himself, with helpful connections on every side. But he could not openly argue against something he had only guessed. If the guess was wrong, he would be shooting at no target and make himself ridiculous in He's eyes. Besides, Hu knew that hints and indirect approaches worked better than plain statements. After a little thought, he found his line of argument. “The governorship of Jiangsu used to be the finest post in the empire,” he suddenly remarked. “Now I should call it the very worst.” He naturally paid attention. “It's true that the post is no longer what it was, but hardly that it has fallen to the bottom.” “I'm only talking at random and seeking your advice.” Speaking slowly, Hu thought of reasons one at a time and offered them as they came. “First, the worst disorder is in Jiangsu. Less territory means less tax revenue.”

zh: “还好，苏松膏腴之地，还在我们手里。”胡雪岩不便说苏松难保，“要保住，也很吃力，刘丽川至今还在上海。这且不去说它，第二，江苏的官太多。“他说，”浙江好的是巡抚独尊！““啊！”何桂清深深点头，“你这话有道理，督抚同城，确是麻烦，不是东风压倒西风，就是西风压倒东风。”“巡抚要压倒总督，怕不大容易，这也不去说它，第三，”胡雪岩又说：“江南大营的向大人，听说很难伺候。云公，有这话没有？”这话当然有的。何桂清心想，江南大营的骄兵悍将，不知凡几，向茶的难侍候，犹其余事。于是本来想在江苏等机会，打算着能接许乃钊的遗缺的心思动摇了。看他默然不语，胡雪岩猜到了他的心思，益发动以危言：“地方官要与城共存亡。我替我们杭州同乡许大人说句私话，如果能够调动一个缺，真正是‘塞翁失马，焉知非福’了。”这句话才真的打动了何桂清，他最胆小，虽然纸上谈兵，豪气万丈，其实最怕打仗。看起来，江苏真的成了末等的缺，何必自讨苦吃，还是进京去吧！主意打定了，却不便明说，只连连点头：“高论极是，佩服之至。”
en: “Not so bad. We still hold the fertile Suzhou–Songjiang country.” Hu could hardly say that even Suzhou and Songjiang might be lost. “Holding it is hard enough. Liu Lichuan is still in Shanghai. But leave that aside. Second, Jiangsu has too many officials. The advantage of Zhejiang is that the governor stands supreme.” “Ah!” He nodded deeply. “There's sense in that. A governor and governor-general in the same city are indeed troublesome. Either the east wind overcomes the west or the west overcomes the east.” “It can hardly be easy for a governor to overcome a governor-general. But leave that aside too. Third, I've heard that General Xiang at the Jiangnan Grand Camp is difficult to serve. Is that true?” Of course it was. He reflected that the camp was full of arrogant troops and unruly commanders; Xiang Rong's difficult temper was the least of it. His intention of waiting in Jiangsu for a chance to succeed Xu began to waver. Seeing him silent, Hu guessed what he was thinking and pressed him with a further warning. “A local official must live or die with his city. Speaking privately on behalf of Governor Xu, my fellow native of Hangzhou, if he could be transferred elsewhere, it might truly be a case of the frontier old man's lost horse proving a blessing in disguise.” This struck home. He was extremely timid. However boldly he discussed warfare on paper, he was terrified of actual fighting. Jiangsu did seem to have become the worst of posts. Why seek trouble? Better go to the capital after all. Having decided, he could not say so openly. He merely nodded repeatedly. “Your argument is entirely right. I admire your insight.”

zh: “我哪里懂什么，不过俗语道得好：”旁观者清。‘不在其位，不关得失，看事情比较清楚。““说得一点不错。”何桂清答道：“我就正要老兄这样的人，多多指点。”“云公这话说得太过分，真叫我脸红。”他趁势站了起来，“我就此告辞了，顺便跟云公辞行。”“怎么？”何桂清顿现怅然之色，“你就这样走了？”“是的，我预备明天一早动身回上海。”“那么……”何桂清沉吟了好半晌说：“我们上海见面吧！那不会太久的。”“是！我一回上海就把款子预备好，随时等云公的招呼。”“还有件事，无论如何，奉托费心。”胡雪岩一愣，随即会意，事实上此事已成功了一半，所以很有把握他说：“云公请放心，一到上海，必有喜信。”何桂清自然高兴。而过分的欣悦，反生感慨，“真想不到，这一次无端与雪岩兄结成知交。”他摇摇头说，“人生在世，都是一个缘字，想想真是不可思议。”胡雪岩跟他的境遇，约略相似，再加上王有龄，三个人天南地北，不知冥冥中是什么力量的驱使？得能聚在一起，象七巧板一样，看似毫不相干，居然拼出一副花样，实在巧妙之至。所以对他的话，深具同感。“云公，说到缘字，还有让你想不到的事。”他紧接着又说，“眼前我不说破，说破了不好玩了。只盼你早则节前，晚则节后，到了上海，我们再叙。”听他如此说法，何桂清便不肯多问，只说：“好，好！我们再叙。良晤非遥，我就不送你了。”“不敢当，我也就不再来辞行了。”他站起身作揖。
en: “What do I know? But as the saying goes, a bystander sees clearly. Without holding the post or having a personal stake in its gains and losses, one can see more plainly.” “Quite true. I need more guidance from men like you.” “You flatter me so much that you make me blush.” Hu took the opportunity to rise. “I must leave now, and take my leave of you before my journey as well.” “What?” He looked disappointed at once. “Are you going already?” “Yes. I mean to return to Shanghai early tomorrow.” “Then...” He considered for a long while. “We'll meet in Shanghai. It won't be very long.” “Certainly. As soon as I'm back, I'll have the money ready and wait for your instructions.” “There is also that other matter. I must ask you, whatever happens, to give it your attention.” Hu was momentarily puzzled, then understood. In fact, half the work was already done, and he could answer confidently. “Don't worry. Once I reach Shanghai, I shall have good news.” He was naturally delighted, and his excessive pleasure turned reflective. “To think that this visit should unexpectedly have made such close friends of us! Life is all a matter of affinity. It's truly beyond understanding.” Hu's circumstances resembled his in some degree. With Wang Youling, they were three men from distant corners of the country, brought together by some unseen force. Like the pieces of a tangram, apparently unrelated, they had combined into a pattern. It was wonderfully ingenious, and Hu felt deep sympathy with He's words. “Speaking of affinity, there's something else that will surprise you. I won't reveal it yet; that would spoil the pleasure. I only hope you'll reach Shanghai before the festival if possible, and shortly after if not. Then we'll talk again.” Hearing this, He would not press. “Very well. We'll talk then. Our next meeting is not far off, so I won't see you off on your journey.” “You needn't trouble yourself. Nor shall I call again to take leave.” Hu rose and bowed.

zh: “你请等一等。”何桂清说完，匆匆又走入书斋，好久，都不见再露面。他是亲笔在写名帖，写信来不及了，只好用名帖，一共七、八张，从苏州到上海，沿路掌管一方的文武官员，都有他的名帖致意，致意是门面话，其实是为胡雪岩作先容。“你备而不用吧！”何桂清把一叠名帖交了过去，“交情深浅，都在措词上看得出来，该用不该用，怎么用法？你自己斟酌。”“有云公这几张名帖，就等于派了百把兵保护，一路上可以睡到上海，多谢，多谢！”“雪轩那里，我另外复信，这里跟浙江，每天都有驿差，方便得很。我就不必麻烦你转信了。”何桂清一面说，一面亲自送客，体制所关，送到二门为止。等胡雪岩回到客栈，他跟着又派人送了四样路菜，一部他新刻的诗槁，另外一个沉甸甸的小木箱，打开来一看，是一只“汽锅”。“难为你家大人想到。”“我家大人交代，”那个叫何福的听差说：“胡大老爷的交情，与众不同，叫我跟胡大老爷请示，若还有事，我就在这里侍候胡大老爷上了船再回去。““不必，不必！我有人，你请回去吧，替我道谢。”说完，在阿巧姐的梳头匣里取了个红封套，红封套甚多，备着赏人用的，轻重不等，最重的是五两一张银票，给何福的就是这一种。
en: “Wait a moment.” He hurried back into his study and did not reappear for some time. He was writing on visiting cards himself. There was no time for letters, so he used seven or eight cards, one for each of the civil and military officials controlling the districts along the route from Suzhou to Shanghai. Ostensibly, they conveyed his regards; in reality, they introduced Hu. “Keep these in reserve,” he said, handing over the little stack. “The wording will tell you how close I am to each man. Judge for yourself which to use, whether to use them and how.” “These cards are as good as sending a hundred soldiers to protect me. I can sleep all the way to Shanghai. Thank you!” “I'll answer Xuexuan separately. Couriers travel between here and Zhejiang every day, so it's easy enough. I needn't trouble you to carry the letter.” As he spoke, He accompanied his guest out. Official propriety allowed him to go no farther than the second gate. After Hu returned to the inn, He sent four dishes for the journey, a copy of his newly printed poems and a small, heavy wooden box. On opening it, Hu found a steam pot. “How thoughtful of your master!” “My master said,” replied the attendant He Fu, “that his friendship with you is unlike any other. He told me to ask whether you need anything. If so, I'm to stay and attend to you until you've boarded your boat.” “No need. I have someone. Please go back and thank him for me.” From A’qiao's dressing case, Hu took a red envelope. There were many there, prepared for tips of varying amounts. The largest contained a five-tael banknote. He gave He Fu one of these.

zh: 这一下，胡雪岩就只有一件事了，等阿巧姐回来。原说午间可到，结果等到日落西山，不见芳踪，反倒是周一鸣又来相伴了。“胡大老爷，真是多亏你栽培。我去请教过人了，说何大人这封八行的力量很够，一定会得个好差使。”他笑嘻嘻地说。“那很好！”胡雪岩也替他高兴，“你得赶快到扬州才好。迟了就没有好差使了。”“不碍。沿运河、长江两岸都要设卡子，差使多得很，抢不光的。我伺候了胡大老爷回上海，再到扬州，最多耽误十天的工夫，不要紧。”看他意思甚诚，而且路上也还要他招呼，胡雪岩就点点头不再多说了。于是又闲谈了一会，同一鸣看胡雪岩有点心神不定的模样，但有些踌躇，再坐下去，怕惹他的厌，如果告辞，丢下他一个人在客栈，更为不妥，想了想又劝他出去喝酒散心。“谢谢，今天不行了。我得等人。”“喔，”周一鸣知道他心神不定的由来了，“是等阿巧姐？”“是啊！她回木渎娘家去，说了中午回来的，至今人面不见，不知是怎么回事？”“此刻不来，今天不会回来了。木渎的航船，早就到了。”“不是搭的航船，自己雇了一只船来回。”“那这样，”周一鸣站起身来，“我到阎门码头上去打听打听看。”“不晓得是哪一条船，怎么打听？”“不要紧！我到那里，一问便知。”“对了！你码头上最熟。”胡雪岩欣然答道，“那就拜托了。”
en: Now Hu had only one thing left to do: wait for A’qiao. She had said she would arrive at noon, but the sun sank without any sign of her. Instead, Zhou returned to keep him company. “Mr Hu, I owe you so much for helping me. I've consulted someone who says His Excellency's letter carries great weight. I'm certain to get a good post.” He was smiling broadly. “Excellent!” Hu was pleased for him. “You ought to get to Yangzhou quickly. Wait too long, and the good posts will be gone.” “Never fear. There'll be stations all along the canal and both banks of the Yangtze. There are too many posts for others to snap them all up. I'll see you back to Shanghai first, then go to Yangzhou. It'll delay me ten days at most. That's nothing.” He was clearly sincere, and Hu would still need his help on the journey, so he nodded and said no more. They talked for a while. Seeing Hu restless, Zhou hesitated. Staying might annoy him, but leaving him alone at the inn would be worse. After considering, he suggested going out for a drink to take his mind off things. “Thank you, but not today. I'm waiting for someone.” “Oh—A’qiao?” Now Zhou understood his uneasiness. “Yes. She went to her parents' home in Mudu and promised to return at noon. There's still no sign of her. I don't know what's happened.” “If she isn't here now, she won't be back today. The regular passenger boat from Mudu arrived long ago.” “She didn't take the regular boat. She hired one for the return journey.” “Then I'll inquire at the Chang Gate wharves.” Zhou stood up. “How can you inquire when we don't know which boat?” “Never mind. Once I'm there, a question will tell me.” “Of course! You know everyone at the wharves. Thank you.”

zh: 等周一鸣走不多时，忽然有个十五六岁的小后生，由金阊栈的店伙领了来见胡雪岩，自道他是潘家跑上房的书僮，奉了他家姨太太之命，“请胡老爷过去，有位堂客，要见胡老爷。”又是姨太太，又是堂客，当着店伙在那里，胡雪岩倒有些尴尬，怕引起误会，传出谣言去，总是烦恼，所以不跟那小后生答话，只向店伙说道：“你们这里，另外有位胡老爷吧？他弄错了！”“不错！”店伙答道，“他说了胡大老爷的官印，上雪下岩，我才领了来了。”“那就奇怪了。”胡雪岩对那小后生说，“苏州我没有姓潘的朋友，更不认得你家姨太太。”“原是木渎来的那位堂客要见胡老爷。”小后生说，“那位堂客是我们姨太太的要好姐妹。”“原来是阿巧姐！”胡雪岩大惑不解，“怎么不回客栈，到了你家？”“那就不清楚了。只说请胡老爷过去见面。”胡雪岩为难了。素昧平生，应人家内眷的邀请，这算是怎么回来？同时阿巧姐有何理由到了潘家？而又叫自己去相会？凡此都是疑窦。以不去为妙。
en: Not long after Zhou left, an inn servant brought in a boy of fifteen or sixteen. He said he was a young attendant who carried messages to the inner quarters of the Pan household. Their mistress had sent him. “Please come over, Mr Hu. A lady would like to see you.” All this talk of mistresses and ladies, with the inn servant listening, embarrassed Hu. It might cause misunderstandings and gossip—always a nuisance. Instead of answering the boy, he addressed the servant. “There's another Mr Hu staying here, isn't there? He has the wrong man.” “No mistake, sir. He gave your name, Xueyan. That's why I brought him in.” “How strange.” Hu turned to the boy. “I have no friend in Suzhou called Pan, and I certainly don't know your mistress.” “It's the lady from Mudu who wants to see you. She's a close friend of our mistress.” “So it's A’qiao!” Hu was utterly puzzled. “Why did she go to your house instead of coming back to the inn?” “I don't know. She only said to ask you to come and see her.” Hu was in a quandary. How could he accept an invitation from the womenfolk of a complete stranger? Why had A’qiao gone to the Pans', and why was she asking him to meet her there? Everything raised doubts. Better not go.

zh: 话虽如此，事情却要弄清楚，真假之间，首先要问阿巧姐，“那位木渎来的堂客，你看见了没有？”他问。“见了的。”“是怎么个样子？”那小后生把阿巧姐的身材、容貌、服饰形容了一遍，果然不错。阿巧姐在潘家这话，看来不假。有了这个了解，事情就好办了，“好的，你到外面等一下。或者去逛一逛再来，我要等个人回来见了面，才能跟你去。”说着，胡雪岩随手在茶几上抓了些零钱给他，“你去买糖吃！”“谢谢胡老爷！”小后生问道，“我歇多少时候再来？”“歇半个时辰。”
en: Even so, he must find out what had happened. To establish whether the story was true, the first thing was to ask about A’qiao. “Have you seen this lady from Mudu?” “Yes.” “What does she look like?” The boy described her figure, features and clothes correctly. It seemed true, then, that A’qiao was at the Pan house. With that established, the next step was easy. “Very well. Wait outside, or go for a walk and come back. I must see someone I'm expecting before I can go with you.” Hu took some small change from the tea table and gave it to him. “Go and buy yourself some sweets.” “Thank you, Mr Hu. When should I come back?” “In an hour.”

zh: 未到半个时辰，等的人到了，是周一鸣，据他打听的结果，阿巧姐的那条船，早在下午三点钟，就已到达。“这有点意思了！看起来不假。”接着，胡雪岩便将那个突如其来的邀请，说了给周一鸣听。“这其中一定有道理。阿巧姐必有不便回来的理由，胡大老爷，我陪了你去。”“你的话不错。不过我不想去，一个人不怕一万，独怕万一。”胡雪岩低声说道，“人心多险，一步错走不得。我平日做人，极为小心，不愿得罪人，但难免遭妒，有人暗中在算计我，亦未可知。别样事都好分辩，就是这种牵涉人家闺阁的事，最要远避。所以，我想请你替我去一趟。”周一鸣久历江湖，各种稀奇古怪的事都经过，心想他是怕着了“仙人跳”，顾虑得倒也有道理。自己替他去走一趟，一样也要小心，当时便点点头说：“我去！去了只把阿巧姐请出来，看她是何话说？”“对了！你问明了立刻来告诉我。”正在谈着，那小后生已转了回来。胡雪岩随便找了个不能分身的理由，来人自无话说，带着周一鸣走了。
en: Before the hour was up, the man he was waiting for returned. It was Zhou. His inquiries showed that A’qiao's boat had arrived as early as three that afternoon. “This is interesting. It seems the story is true.” Hu then told him about the unexpected invitation. “There must be a reason. A’qiao must have some difficulty about returning here. I'll go with you.” “You're right, but I don't want to go. It's the one chance in ten thousand that a man must fear.” Lowering his voice, Hu continued, “People can be treacherous. One wrong step may ruin everything. I'm always careful and try to offend no one, but I can't avoid jealousy. Someone may be plotting against me. Other matters can be explained. Anything involving the women's quarters of another household is best kept far away from. I'd like you to go for me.” Zhou had long experience of the world and had seen every kind of strange affair. Hu was afraid of an extortion trap involving a woman, he thought, and the concern was reasonable. He too must be careful if he went in Hu's place. He nodded. “I'll go. I'll simply ask A’qiao to come out and hear what she has to say.” “Exactly. Find out and come straight back to tell me.” As they spoke, the boy returned. Hu gave some convenient reason why he could not leave. The messenger could hardly object and took Zhou away.

zh: 这一走，过了个把时辰，才见他回来，“阿巧姐的话很多，有些事，我也弄不清楚。”周一鸣略停一停，整理一下思绪，要言不烦地说：“阿巧姐夫家派了人，从木渎跟了她到这里，看样子是来找麻烦。阿巧姐不愿回这里，就是不愿意让他们发现她落脚的地方。阿巧姐说有好些话一定要跟胡大老爷你当面谈。她怕跟来的人，在潘家附近守着，此刻不敢出门，到半夜里叫我去接了她来。”“喔！”胡雪岩深为诧异，“据我知道，她夫家老实得很。怎有此事？”这话在周一鸣无可赞一词，只这样说，“反正见了面就知道了。”“慢点！”胡雪岩双目炯炯，神色凛然，“不能去接她！万一为人跟踪，明天告我个拐带良家妇女，这个面子我丢不起。老周，我问你，那潘家是怎么回事？”“苏州潘家有两潘，一潘是‘贵潘’，一潘是‘富潘’，阿巧姐的那一家，是富潘的同族。阿巧姐的小姐妹，是他家的姨太太，太太故世了，姨太太当家，所以能够作主，把阿巧姐留了下来往。”“潘家的男主人，叫啥？你晓得不晓得。”“不晓得。”“不晓得也不碍。”胡雪岩说，“等我去拜他家男主人，当面说明经过，把阿巧姐找了出来，就当着他家男主人谈好了。不过，这一下，要委屈你了。“这话周一鸣明白，是要他权且充任报帖的家人，这也无所谓，他很爽快地答应：“我伺候胡大老爷去。”于是雇好一顶轿子，周一鸣持着拜匣，跟随胡雪岩到了潘家。帖子一投进去，潘家的男主人莫名其妙，但他的姨太太心里明白，说了经过，方始恍然，立刻吩咐接见。
en: It was some two hours before Zhou returned. “A’qiao had a great deal to say. There are things I don't fully understand.” He paused to collect his thoughts, then explained briefly. “Her husband's family sent someone who followed her here from Mudu. They seem to be looking for trouble. She didn't come back because she didn't want them to discover where she's staying. She says there are many things she must discuss with you in person. She's afraid the people following her are watching near the Pans', so she dare not leave now. She wants me to fetch her at midnight.” “Oh!” Hu was deeply surprised. “As far as I know, her husband's family are very docile. How can this be?” Zhou could offer no opinion. “You'll know when you see her.” “Wait!” Hu's eyes flashed, and his expression became stern. “You mustn't fetch her. If someone follows and accuses me tomorrow of abducting a respectable married woman, I can't afford that disgrace. Old Zhou, tell me about this Pan family.” “There are two prominent Pan families in Suzhou: the ‘Noble Pans’ and the ‘Rich Pans’. This household belongs to the same clan as the Rich Pans. A’qiao's friend is the master's concubine. His principal wife has died, so the concubine runs the household. That's why she can decide to let A’qiao stay.” “What's the master's name? Do you know?” “No.” “That doesn't matter. I'll call on him and explain what has happened. Then we can ask A’qiao to come out and talk in his presence. But this will mean asking you to accept a humble role.” Zhou understood: he was to act for the moment as a servant presenting Hu's visiting card. He did not mind and readily agreed. “I'll attend you.” They hired a sedan chair. Carrying the card case, Zhou accompanied Hu to the Pan house. When the card was brought in, the master was bewildered. His concubine understood, however, and explained. Once he grasped the situation, he immediately ordered that the visitor be received.
